summary: Joachim Wach was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Freiberg, Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, Leiden, Leipzig (Dissertation 1922), and Heidelberg. He taught at Leipzig, Brown University (1935–1946), and the University of Chicago (Professor, 1945–1955).

Joan Jiko Halifax is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Newcomb College, Miami, and Union Institute (PhD 1973), she held posts at Columbia, Harvard, and the Library of Congress (2011), and founded the Upaya Zen Center.

Joan Mascaró was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Cambridge from circa 1920 to 1924. In 1933, he served as Professor of English at the University of Barcelona.

Joanna Bialek is a Tibetology and linguistics scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Marburg in 2016. Her posts include Humboldt University of Berlin (2017–2022), Trinity College Dublin (2024–2026), and a 2026 postdoc at the University of Munich.
Joanna Cook is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She studied under advisor James Laidlaw and held a post at Christ's College, Cambridge.

Joanna Gottfried Williams was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University (1960–1969). She served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1970 to 2005.

Joanna Grela works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at INALCO, Jagiellonian University (PhD 2004), and SWPS University (habilitation 2016). In 2006, she became a professor at Jagiellonian University.

Joanna Jurewicz is an Indology, philosophy, and linguistics scholar. She was appointed Chair of South Asia Studies at the University of Warsaw in 1989 and held a post attested in 2021 at the University of South Africa.

Joanna Macy is a religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Wellesley College from circa 1946 to 1950 and completed studies at Syracuse University between circa 1974 and 1978.

Joanne Punzo Waghorne is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Chicago (circa 1971–1976). She held academic posts at UMass Boston, Bowdoin College, UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University.

Joannes van der Vliet was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at Leiden University (PhD circa 1874). He was docent of Sanskrit at Amsterdam (1890) and professor of Latin at Utrecht (1891–1892).
Joanny Grosset was an Indologist who earned his Licencié-ès-lettres at the University of Lyon and studied under Paul Regnaud from circa 1885 to 1895.

Joaquim Heliodoro da Cunha Rivara was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Coimbra from 1824 to 1836. He served as a teacher and librarian at Liceu de Évora from circa 1838 to 1855.

Jochem Schindler was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied under Heinz Kronasser at Vienna and earned his PhD at Würzburg. He taught at Harvard (1974–1987) and served as a professor at the University of Vienna from 1987.

Joe Bransford Wilson works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Wisconsin, Virginia (PhD 1984), UNF, FGCU, and Florida, he studied with Geshe Lhundup Sopa and taught at Virginia (1981–1985) and UNC Wilmington.

Joe Cribb is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at the University of London. He was Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010) and President of the Royal Numismatic Society.
Joe Currie is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He has held a post at Harvard University, where he is also attested as a PhD candidate in 2026.

Joel Bordeaux is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at Columbia in 2015. He held posts at Colgate, Stony Brook, Leiden (2020–2023), Utrecht (2023–2025), and Erasmus University Rotterdam (2025).

Joel Peter Brereton is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Stanley Insler. He held positions at the University of Missouri (1999–2000) and the University of Texas at Austin, where he was appointed professor in 2004.

Joel Tatelman is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 1996. He held an attested post at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1997–1998.
